title: Neuron Explorer
description: Interactive labeled neuron with an oligodendrocyte, an astrocyte, and a blood vessel. Hovering, clicking, or choosing a part shows its job. A Send signal button animates a signal down a myelinated axon; a Remove myelin (MS) option strips myelin from 1 to 4 segments so students can see the signal slow, fade, and fail, as in multiple sclerosis.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: Neuroscience
learningObjectives: Identify the dendrites, cell body (soma), axon hillock, axon, myelin sheath, nodes of Ranvier, and axon terminals of a neuron and state the job of each.
Describe the jobs of an oligodendrocyte and an astrocyte.
Explain why a myelinated axon carries signals faster and why losing myelin, as in multiple sclerosis, can slow a signal or block it.
prerequisites: Basic cell structure: nucleus, cell membrane, and proteins
The idea that cells can carry electrical charge using ions (Chapter 1, Section 1.2)
keyQuestions: What does each part of a neuron do as a message passes through it?
Why does a signal travel faster along an axon wrapped in myelin?
What happens to a signal when a stretch of myelin is destroyed, and how does that explain symptoms of multiple sclerosis?
misconceptions: The nervous system is made only of neurons (glial cells are about as numerous as neurons).
Myelin is part of the neuron itself (it is made by glial cells: oligodendrocytes in the CNS and Schwann cells in the PNS).
Losing myelin always stops a signal completely (small patches may only slow it; larger patches can block it).

controls.label: Send signal
controls.description: Fires a new signal at the start of the axon.

controls.label: Pause / Resume
controls.description: Freezes or continues the traveling signal.

controls.label: Remove myelin (MS)
controls.description: Strips myelin from the chosen number of segments, starting under the oligodendrocyte.

controls.label: Damaged segments
controls.description: How many of the six myelinated segments lose their myelin when the MS option is checked.

controls.label: Explore a part
controls.description: Keyboard-friendly way to show any part's job in the info panel.

assumptions: A healthy myelinated segment is crossed in 8 animation frames; a demyelinated segment takes 40 frames.
In a demyelinated stretch, signal strength falls by a factor of 0.55 per segment crossed.
A healthy node renews the signal to 100% if it arrives with at least 25% strength; below 25% the signal is blocked.
limitations: Speeds, fading rate, and threshold are illustrative and chosen to show the pattern, not taken from a real nerve.
The model does not show ion channels or the action potential waveform (covered in Chapter 2).
Real MS lesions vary in size, location, and severity; six segments is a teaching simplification.

accessibility: describe() text for screen readers; every part can be chosen from a dropdown menu without a mouse
